text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.4% today as oil prices slipped on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East, easing some of the geopolitical premium that had been supporting crude. The stock is down from its $484.92 high two weeks ago, though it remains up 5.94% over that span — a reflection of the volatile and ultimately uncertain oil market it operates in. US oil sits at $107.89 per barrel, and refineries are running at 93.4% capacity, which is solid but not exceptional.

The broader picture is a tug-of-war between supply concerns and demand uncertainty. Recent attacks on Russian oil facilities by Ukraine and Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure have kept prices elevated, but traders are also factoring in the possibility of diplomatic breakthroughs that could ease tensions and lower crude costs — the latter prospect weighing on the stock today. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices can be a double-edged sword: margins may shrink, though the company benefits from reduced input costs when processing crude into gasoline and diesel.
